p: Five nets means you can bring a properly big crowd and still keep everyone busy, but it pays to think about how you split them. Mixing confident batters with first-timers in each net keeps the scores close and the banter flowing. Nominate someone to keep things moving, as there's always one person who wants just one more go. Trainers and loose clothes are the order of the day, and if you're coming straight from the office, a spare top in your bag won't go amiss.

Take the competition seriously enough to be fun, but not so seriously that anyone pulls a hamstring. Short, sharp sessions with a break for food and drink in the middle usually beat batting non-stop. If some of your group would rather watch, the terrace and screens give them somewhere comfy to cheer from.

Bermondsey Street itself is well worth a wander before or after. It's one of those London streets that still feels like a neighbourhood, with independent restaurants, pubs and galleries, and it's home to the Fashion and Textile Museum, which puts on changing exhibitions through the year. Head towards the river and you'll find Hay's Galleria, the Thames path and great views of Tower Bridge. Southwark Cathedral and the food stalls of Borough Market are a short walk west, and HMS Belfast is moored just along the bank if you've got history fans in tow.
